record.original_title: Projet de loi portant mise en oeuvre de certaines dispositions du règlement (UE) 2024/1689 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 13 juin 2024 établissant des règles harmonisées concernant l'intelligence artificielle et modifiant les règlements (CE) n° 300/2008, (UE) n° 167/2013, (UE) n° 168/2013, (UE) 2018/858, (UE) 2018/1139 et (UE) 2019/2144 et les directives 2014/90/UE, (UE) 2016/797 et (UE) 2020/1828 (règlement sur l'intelligence artificielle) et portant modification de : 1° la loi du 1er août 2018 portant organisation de la Commission nationale pour la protection des données et du régime général sur la protection des données ; 2° la loi modifiée du 23 décembre 1998 portant création d'une commission de surveillance du secteur financier ; 3° la loi modifiée du 7 décembre 2015 sur le secteur des assurances
record.notes: Approved by the Government in council on 29 November 2024 and deposited by Elisabeth Margue, Minister Delegate to the Prime Minister for Media and Connectivity, on 23 December 2024; referred on 16 January 2025 to the Committee on Media and Communications, which appointed Félix Eischen rapporteur on 3 June 2025. Twelve opinions are on file, from the CSSF, ILNAS, FEDIL, the Chamber of Employees, ALIA, the Chambers of Commerce and Trades, the Competition Authority, the CNPD, the ILR, the Bar Council, the judicial control authority (23 January 2026) and the Council of State (10 July 2026, No 62.024). The Council of State raised formal objections, among them to the missing split of notifying tasks between ILNAS and the Government Commissioner (renamed Government Commissioner for Data Sovereignty by a law of 19 December 2025), to the CSSF's remit unless limited as Article 74(6) of the AI Act requires, to the regulatory and complaint-handling provisions of Article 9 and to inexact references in Article 14. As of the dossier's last update on 10 July 2026 the bill was in committee and had not been voted. The bill sets 2 August 2026 as the deadline for the CNPD's first regulatory sandbox, treats a real-world testing plan as approved when the market surveillance authority has not answered within 30 days, and follows the AI Act's fine ceilings (EUR 35 million or 7%, 15 million or 3%, 7.5 million or 1% of worldwide turnover).

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the Chamber of Deputies dossier page for bill 8476 (chd.lu, snapshot of 12 October 2026), which gives the title, type, author, deposit date, committee, rapporteur, the twelve opinions and the stage 'En commission' with the last update on 10 July 2026; the deposit document (wdocs-pub.chd.lu, stored as the record's secondary source), with the Government's decision of 29 November 2024, the deposit order of 23 December 2024 and the bill's 22 articles; the consolidated dossier created on 10 July 2026, which includes every opinion and the Council of State's opinion No 62.024; and ILNAS's opinion. On 17 October 2026 chd.lu's robots.txt refused the dossier page, so the stage cannot be checked after 12 October 2026. The Commission's list of market surveillance authorities cited in version 1 is not stored, and its mention was removed. No English text of the bill was found.
